items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: And then about two weeks later they killed King Abdullah.

ctx.x: I generally know what's happening, yes. He says, well, do you know we're going to be all right, soon. Then everyday would say, why don't you come and visit us. Took me to the mosque. Said, I want you to learn the Arabic. See, this happened to me all the time.

He said, I'm going to send you to Egypt and you go to school and learn that, we're going to get straight. And then the next day he said, no more of that, because we're going to be going ahead, we're going to be doing something to him. I said (Inaudible). He said, we're going to send you to Transjordan. And then about two weeks later they killed King Abdullah. He said, no, you'd better wait. I said, yeah, I'm going to wait.

And then, I remember it was one Tuesday night. The paper said that Tunisia is at liberty. And this man come in and (inaudible) in France you've got -- cars can go in the middle of the street, and you've got a street in the middle, too. And cars can park on the sidewalk (inaudible) got an island. With that island, you park your car. And we sit on them benches and this man cried. He cried (inaudible). And he went to Tunisia and became the minister of state of foreign affairs. And he used to write me often. I was…
